chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The worst of people in the presence of Allah on the Day of Judgment are those who are honored out of fear of their evil.'

key_terms.اتِّقَاءَ شَرِّهِمْ: Out of fear of their evil

ai.seo_question: Who are the worst people in the sight of Allah on the Day of Judgment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this hadith from *Al-Kafi* critiques the social phenomenon of *ittiqāʾ al-sharr* (fearing one's evil), where respect is granted based on power or potential harm rather than moral merit. It serves as a warning against superficial honor and highlights the divine preference for those whose status is rooted in genuine virtue rather than the fear of their capacity to cause damage.
